thesis: This episode argues that investors should focus on 'great businesses with great people and long runways' like Amazon, Costco, and Berkshire Hathaway, while avoiding overvalued or failing companies like Xerox and Polaroid. It suggests that a long-term strategy of holding these high-quality stocks can significantly outperform the market, even if other positions in the portfolio fail.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Titan is still firing on all cylinders and is embryonic in its growth and development.
claims.quote: And the amazing thing about Titan is that it's still firing on all cylinders. And it's actually, even today, in my opinion, still embryonic in its growth and development.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests that Amazon was a radical change and worked out very well, even if everything else in the portfolio went to zero.
claims.quote: And Amazon was, I think, about before the split, it was 115th of the price price it is today. I mean, it was a radical change. And anyway, what Nick and Zach did for their own portfolio is they allocated a third each to these three companies.

claims.claim: The speaker includes Costco as one of the three stocks to buy equally, suggesting a long-term hold strategy.
claims.quote: three stocks equally, Amazon, Costco, and Berkshire. So now he's telling you that you don't need to pay me any fees anymore. And you just buy these three stocks and you don't touch it for 10 years.
